items.title: Bill Huntington Interview, 1961-12-27
items.q: I think Bunk had it, uh, I think Jelly Roll had it.

ctx.x: Well, it's more or less that Lewis band that, that were your favorite out of that era.

Yeah, well, because there was nobody else to listen to, except on records. Uh, when I played with Barnes, there were very few times when his chops were up, you know, where he'd play something that was really meaningful. When he did, you know, it would really get to me. And, uh, it was really something to listen to. And so many of the other drummers would rush and, uh, retard or have some kind of problem here or there, you know. Same thing with the other instrumentalists. And then from what Lawrence was telling…

What did he teach you in, uh, in the very fundamental technical things I'm talking about? Uh, not just, just start at the beginning, before you ever got into anything like harmony, just, how to hold your banjo and how to stroke it.
